content.text: No assignment of AbbVie IP or data to Harpoon exists anywhere in the agreement, and the joint-IP regime carries free exploitation rights. This is compliant.

input.quote: Subject to the licenses and rights of reference granted under Sections 5.1 and 5.2 and, in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder, each Party shall have the right to Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party.
input.rationale: The IP architecture protects our position. Section 7.1.1 (p0427–p0428) gives each Party sole ownership of Information, inventions, Patents and other IP made by or on behalf of it, plus everything it already owns or Controls, so AbbVie retains its own inventions and pre-existing IP with no assignment to Harpoon. Section 7.1.4(a) (p0432) requires each Party's personnel and subcontractors to assign their results to that Party, which channels work product to AbbVie rather than away from it. On data, Section 3.8.2(c) (p0327) makes all Regulatory Documentation, Regulatory Approvals and Product Labeling for the Licensed Compounds/Products the sole property of AbbVie, with Harpoon obliged to execute confirmatory assignments — i.e. we own the dossier we pay for. Section 5.6.2 (p0364) confirms no implied licence of AbbVie Patents or AbbVie Know-How, and the only grant to Harpoon (Section 5.2) is a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free, non-sublicensable licence limited to performing the Initial Development Plan. Access to Harpoon's side is delivered by the exclusive licences in Section 5.1.3, with Harpoon keeping its platform technology — which the playbook expressly accepts.
